description: Save to Stuga. Use when the user says "Save to Stuga" or the same in their language ("存到 Stuga", "Stugaに保存", "Stuga에 저장", "In Stuga speichern", "Enregistrer dans Stuga", "Guardar en Stuga", "Salvar no Stuga"), "remember this in Stuga", or otherwise asks you to keep something in Stuga for later — never your own memory instead. This tool writes no text: it finds where each point belongs, in the pages the user can read (the first call in a workspace makes the user's My notes folder there). `points`: 1 to 20, each `text`, an optional `topic`, and `source` (the meeting, email or document it came from, and when, kept out of `text`; none for what the user told you). `user` is whom you act for, by their Stuga name. For each point it returns `candidates`, best first: pages the user can edit (`kind: "page"`: doc_id, title, folder path, the `section` heading it fits under — null for the page's opening, or a page whose title alone fits — why, an excerpt), rows of tables the user can edit (`kind: "row"`: the database, `table`, the `row` the point names by its title cell — null for a new row — and `fills`, the columns it fills, each cell as it reads now with `already_saved`, `possibly_replaces` or `waiting`) and folders a new page on it belongs in (`kind: "new_page"`), each with `review`: whether a write there applies at once or waits for the user's or a colleague's approval; `already_saved` (sentences that already say it), `possibly_replaces` (sentences it may make untrue, or, with hint "likely_duplicate", that may say it already: compare before writing), and a `note` when only words were matched and no page found is about it: its page may be written in another language. `home` is the user's own "My notes" folder in the workspace, where their own notes go (`home.shared`: whether anyone else reads it now); `home.pages` are the pages in it. `instructions` is what people wrote for agents about these places: follow it. THEN, for each point not already saved: read the best place with `markdown` action:read, and write — ONE change for the whole save: `change_title` on your first write, its `change_id` on every other — `markdown_edit` str_replace when it corrects or updates a sentence there (change that sentence: never leave the old and the new both standing), `markdown_append` with `heading` to add a new fact under the right section, or `docs_create` for a new page (in the `new_page` folder, or the folder whose instructions say it belongs, else in My notes: `home.folder_id`, reusing a page of `home.pages` on the same topic), then `markdown_append` to fill it. TABLES: a fact a table's columns name (a contact, a plan, a date, an amount) goes in its row, prose (a decision, a reason, how something is done) in a page. For a `row` candidate write `databases_change` action:update_rows (`updates`: [{_id: the row's `row_id`, values: {column: value}}]) to fill or correct its cells, a cell that holds another value changed in place, never a second row; for `row: null`, `databases_add` action:insert_rows with its title column named; both in the same change. A `waiting` cell or a `waiting_row` is proposed already: tell the user it waits instead of writing it again. WHO AND WHEN: for what the user tells you directly, write no name and no date with it (no "per …", "noted by …"): Stuga's version history records who changed what and when. For a point from a meeting, an email or a document, give that as its `source` and cite it in the text as the place's instructions ask, else in a few words after the fact ("(customer sync, 2026-10-21)"); never attribute it to the user, and never invent one. A point from a page in Stuga is cited as that page: `markdown_edit` action:cited_edits with a citation naming its `doc_id`, only a page you read here (any other is refused, `citation_not_found`), so the wiki can tell when that page changes and this one needs checking. WRITING: keep each point in the language of what it came from (a chat in Chinese gives points in Chinese) or of the page it belongs on, never translated; one point is one fact; names instead of pronouns, and the user, when a point is about them ("I'm on call on Mondays"), by their Stuga name (`user.name`), never a name taken from a file path, an email address or your own memory; the conclusion, never the raw text or "the email says…"; only what will still matter in six months; never invent a point to have something to save; a correction edits the old sentence. AFTERWARDS tell the user what you saved and where (with links), what was already there, and what waits for their or a colleague's approval; when you wrote nothing, say that nothing was saved, never that it was saved or recorded.

points.description: The points to save, 1 to 20; one point is a list of one.

source.description: Where it came from, and when, when that is not the user telling you: "customer sync, 2026-10-21", "email from Sam, 2026-10-18", "the onboarding handbook". Omit it for what the user told you directly; never guess one.

text.description: One fact, complete on its own, in about 15 to 80 words: names instead of pronouns, the conclusion, never the raw text, and no source or date of telling; in the language of what it came from or of the page it belongs on.

topic.description: What the fact is about (Refunds, Hiring, the Acme account), never the meeting or email it came from.

workspace_id.description: The workspace to act in: a `workspace_id` from `workspaces` action:list, which also says which node it is on.

name: remember
title: Save to Stuga
